_comment: Deliberate, accepted deviations from the terraform declaration (ENG-433). An entry here does NOT hide a finding — check_provision_parity.py still prints it, marked ACCEPTED with its reason, and only stops it failing the run. The point is that a check carrying a permanent known failure trains people to ignore it, while a check that can never be silenced gets bypassed instead. Both fail; an explicit, dated, reasoned exception is the honest middle. Every entry needs a reason, a date and an owner — an exception with no reason is indistinguishable from a bug someone gave up on.
_schema: match = substring of the failure line. Keep it specific enough to not swallow a future, different finding.

exceptions.match: WIDER THAN SPEC: serviceAccount:vault-sa@igniteiq-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com holds roles/bigquery.dataViewer at PROJECT level
exceptions.reason: Every hand-provisioned tenant holds this at project level rather than dataset-scoped on `ontology` as iam.tf declares — I introduced it on Eco by copying Reynolds, and Reynolds and Tapps already had it, so the drift predates Eco. Fixing it requires REVOKING a live binding on the query engine's identity, and Ryan's standing rule is that no IAM revoke happens without his approval (additive only). The dataset-scoped grant the module declares has been added additively to eco/reynolds/tapps, so Vault's access is now correct-and-also-wider rather than wrong. Revoking the project-level binding is the remaining step and is deliberately deferred.
exceptions.review: Revisit with the Vault least-privilege pass. Verify in a non-prod tenant first: vault-sa reads ONLY ontology today, but a dashboard or agent querying a forge_* or depot_raw table directly would break on revoke, and that has not been measured.

exceptions.reason: Airworks is the last abctl-VM holdout (ENG-281) and was never provisioned by this module. It has no depot-sa at all — ingestion runs on a VM with a service-account KEY (`airbyte-sa-key` in its GSM) rather than Workload Identity. So these are architectural non-matches, not missing grants. They resolve when Airworks migrates to Depot-on-GKE, at which point the exception should be DELETED rather than updated.
exceptions.review: Delete on ENG-281 completion. Note the VM path needs an SA key, which Eco's org forbids via iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation — a tenant with that policy could not run the abctl path at all.

exceptions.reason: Redwood is the internal demo tenant with NO live Depot sync by design (its 29 dbt source-freshness failures are expected for the same reason). There is no ingestion runtime to grant, so depot-sa legitimately does not exist. Not a customer project.
exceptions.accepted_by: Ryan (2026-08-04, 'redwood is demo but you can check it')
exceptions.review: Permanent while Redwood stays a static demo. If it ever gets a live sync, delete this.

exceptions.reason: Airworks' relay exists (depot-relay-514287425201) and its shared secret is held in the Platform DB (Organization.depotRelaySecret), not in the customer's GSM — it predates this module, which generates the value and stores it project-side. Creating an EMPTY shell of that name would be worse than absent: it would look authoritative while holding nothing. Left alone deliberately.
exceptions.review: Resolve with ENG-281's migration, which would provision the relay through the module.

exceptions.reason: customer-deployer cannot read airworks' ontology dataset ACL (403) — it holds no dataset-level access on a project it did not provision. So parity for vault-sa's dataset-scoped grant is UNKNOWN there, not confirmed absent. Recorded as accepted so the run is not permanently red, but it is explicitly an unverified item, not a passing one.
exceptions.review: Needs an identity with dataset read on airworks. Resolve when ENG-281 migrates it, or grant customer-deployer read there.

exceptions.reason: Jolly granted the posture auditor on 2026-08-05 from the EIGHT-permission role definition, and eight turned out to be one short: it lacks secretmanager.secrets.getIamPolicy, which reads a secret's access list. So parity for depot-sa's secretAccessor on the four jolly-servicetitan-* secrets is UNKNOWN, not confirmed absent. Covers exactly four lines — app-key, client-id, client-secret, tenant-id. The ninth permission was added to iam_auditor.tf and roles/tenant_posture_auditor.yaml the same day, so every FUTURE tenant is provisioned able to verify this; Jolly's live role predates that and is not retroactively updated. Accepted rather than re-asking Jolly for a second grant one day after the first, because their ingestion is running — which is stronger evidence that depot-sa can read those credentials than reading the policy would be. This is an UNVERIFIED item, not a passing one.
exceptions.accepted_by: Ryan (2026-08-06, 'add the exception entry to parity-exceptions.json for jolly')
exceptions.review: DELETE — do not widen — as soon as Jolly's role carries the ninth permission, by either route: `gcloud iam roles update tenantPostureAuditor --project=ignite-iq --add-permissions=secretmanager.secrets.getIamPolicy`, or their next terraform apply from the updated module. ⚠️ The match is name-prefixed rather than anchored on "'s IAM policy", so it would also swallow a DIFFERENT failure mentioning those secrets — if the four accepted lines ever change shape, tighten it instead of leaving it broad.
